title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a working note. It is page 32 of the typescript of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), stamped 350 and filed among the 1975–76 notes on divided-power De Rham complexes. The neighbouring pages are handwritten computations on coalgebras C, comodules and the functors V(C), so the typescript sheet was presumably kept or reused as scrap.

Content: Proposition 3.5, the Galois criterion for semi-stable reduction.

Setting: S is a trait (spectrum of a discrete valuation ring) with fraction field K, and A_K is an abelian variety over K. One may pass to the henselisation of S.
- U = T_ℓ(A_K(K̄)) is the ℓ-adic Tate module, ℓ different from the residue characteristic.
- I is the inertia group.
- V = U^I is the fixed part; it identifies with the Tate module of the special fibre of the Néron model.
- W ⊂ V is the toric part.
- V^⊥ is the orthogonal of V for the Weil pairing. This pairs U with the Tate module of the dual abelian variety; the notation tacitly identifies the two, or keeps the primes implicit.

The following are equivalent:
- (i) A_K has semi-stable reduction, i.e. the identity component of the special fibre of the Néron model has no unipotent part (λ = 0 in the notation of 2.1.9).
- (ii) V ⊂ V^⊥.
- (iii) W = V^⊥.
- (iv) I acts unipotently of level 2: there is an I-stable U' such that I acts trivially on U' and on U/U'.

Proof:
- (i)⇔(ii): the dimension formula (2.5.5) relates λ to rank(V) − rank(V ∩ V^⊥), so λ = 0 means V = V ∩ V^⊥.
- (ii)⇔(iii): the orthogonality theorem 2.4 gives W = V ∩ V^⊥.
- (iv)⇔(ii): level-2 unipotence means I acts trivially on U/U^I = U/V. Dually, I then acts trivially on V^⊥, i.e. V^⊥ ⊂ U^I = V. This is (ii) on the dual side, and is symmetric via a polarisation.

Remark 3.5.1 begins: (ii) and (iv) depend only on the I-action on U ⊗ Q_ℓ, and are stable under base change.

Purpose: this is the ℓ-adic criterion used to deduce the semi-stable reduction theorem (after a finite extension, via the Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich style argument and the quasi-unipotence of inertia).
errors: In the proof of (iv)⇒(ii) the typescript says that (iv) means 'I opère trivialement sur U^I = V'. That statement is tautological. The intended statement is that I acts trivially on the quotient U/U^I = U/V; by duality, trivial action on U/V is equivalent to trivial action on V^⊥.

The step 'V^⊥ ⊂ U^I = V' tacitly identifies the Tate module of A with that of the dual abelian variety. This is harmless (one can use a polarisation, or state everything with primes), but it is not stated here.
The inclusion V^⊥ ⊂ V yields (ii) V ⊂ V^⊥ only after using the symmetric statement for the dual, or a rank argument. The typescript compresses this step.

ideas.what: Galois (ℓ-adic) criterion for semi-stable reduction: semi-stable if and only if inertia acts unipotently of level 2 on T_ℓ, equivalently V ⊂ V^⊥, equivalently W = V^⊥.
Orthogonality theorem W = V ∩ V^⊥ (toric part as the orthogonal of the fixed part under the Weil pairing).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of published SGA 7 IX (Prop. 3.5), which is standard and fully credited to Grothendieck. Its only archival interest is that it was filed, presumably as scrap paper, among the 1976 coalgebra notes.
